116	## 1. When this applies
117	
118	An app screen is worked in rather than read. This chapter covers:
119	
120	- dashboards and overviews: a seller's day, a project's health, a publication's growth;
121	- admin and back office: members, orders, events, a catalogue;
122	- analytics and reports, including a generated report with no app around it;
123	- settings and billing;
124	- list screens to work through: inboxes, queues, tables with filters;
125	- wallets and finance homes;
126	- builders and editors: flow, form and page builders, canvases;
127	- the detail page of one object: an event, a deployment, a customer.
128	
129	A product site that shows its interface is a page; the interface fragments on it follow these rules
130	for their insides (mark each fragment's root with `data-ui`). When a request holds both, build each
131	with its own run and share one palette and one typeface.
132	
133	The study is 23 desktop screens. It has no phone screens, no loading or error states, one settings
134	page, no inbox and no dense operations table (the densest screen shows about 120 data points). Where a
135	rule below goes past the study, it says **house rule**.
136	
137	## 2. The run for an app screen
138	
139	Do these in order. The first three steps decide whether the screen is any good.
140	
141	### 2.1 Inventory the data and the jobs
142	
143	The page run inventories the subject's world; an app screen inventories its data. Write in your notes,
144	in 8 to 12 lines:
145	
146	- **the objects** the screen shows (deployments, invoices, members, events, conversations) and their
147	  fields, with units;
148	- **realistic magnitudes**: how many objects, a typical amount, the range of a rate, how values move
149	  over a day, a month, a year, and for a new account how small they really are;
150	- **the people**: who opens this screen, how often (a glance once a day, or an eight-hour session),
151	  on what device;
152	- **the jobs**: what they do next from here (approve, reply, pay, ship, invite), and which job comes
153	  up most;
154	- **the product's own things**: its name and mark, the workspace or account it is scoped to, the people
155	  in it (two partners, a team of six, the club's members), and the objects people recognise by sight
156	  (product photographs in a shop, cover art in a media tool, a map of the route). These are what make
157	  a screen belong to this product instead of to a template; plan where each one appears.
158	
159	Then write the data itself: a small dataset in a JSON or JS file that the screen renders from, with
160	believable names, amounts that add up to their totals, dates in order and a unit on every figure.
161	Totals are computed from the rows, never typed in separately. Small numbers stay small: the studied
162	screens show new accounts with 1, 6 or 9 of something, drawn honestly at their real size. Write the
163	figures that must agree as assertions in the data file (`console.assert(sold - cancelled === rsvps)`,
164	the bins sum to the total, the parts to the whole) and read the console: in testing, a ticket table
165	that did not reconcile with its own KPI cost a judge's trust in the whole screen. Checks that need
166	computed values (allowance after a request, cover per day) go in the script that computes them.
167	
168	**Data that tells the truth** (house rules, from testing; judges checked every one of these):
169	
170	- **A fact shown twice is one variable.** A time window, a total or a state that appears in two cards
171	  (the battery full 13:30-16:30 in the KPI label, the shaded span and the battery card) is one value in
172	  the data file, and the copy and the chart annotation are both built from it. Two cards that
173	  disagree by half an hour cost more trust than a missing card.
174	- **Totals and deltas come from the parts as shown.** Sum the rounded pennies the screen displays,
175	  never round the unrounded total separately: £21.68 + £8.34 − £3.81 is £26.21, and a screen that
176	  says £26.22 is caught. A change is the difference of the two values on screen (£5.28 against
177	  £5.22 is +£0.06, not +£0.07).
178	- **Every relative figure names its baseline** in the same phrase: "3 h 40 m before close", "45 m
179	  earlier than last Sunday", "+5 on the usual Monday". "Early", "up" or a bare "+5" next to another
180	  time or figure reads as measured against that one.
181	- **One name per time.** Shops close at 15:00 and the tills are cashed up at 15:12; the header and
182	  the card use the same words for the same moment, and an error state rewrites the status line.
183	- **If a caption has to say which bars are which, encode it in the chart instead**: a marked period in
184	  a second tone with its own legend entry, a signed axis, a label on the mark.
185	
186	### 2.2 Name the screen's one question
187	
188	Every screen answers one question first: "Did today's sales come in?", "Which deploy broke?", "Who is
189	waiting for a reply?", "How much of this month's plan is left?". Write it in one line. It decides
190	three things:
191	
192	- **what is biggest.** In the study the largest block is always the one that carries the screen's
193	  question, whatever form it takes (a chart, a plan, a ring, a list). The same holds for figures:
194	  the largest figure on the screen answers the question the title row's sentence answers. In testing,
195	  an 88% sun ratio at 32px out-shouted the 24px charging window the title led with;
196	- **what comes first** in the reading order;
197	- **what is left out.** The studied settings page shows three usage numbers and links to the
198	  analytics screen instead of drawing a chart; four screens draw no chart at all because a few
199	  numbers say it.
200	
201	Then name the screen's **one finding**: the fact in today's data that most needs attention ("9 no-shows
202	while 8 people waited for a place", "the 23:28 deploy doubled the error rate", "eating out is £36 over").
203	Put it where it is read first, as the line under the title or the subline of the headline figure,
204	next to the action it drives. In testing, the finding that mattered sat in a 14px caption at the
205	bottom of a card and the screen read as flat.
206	
207	**Do not rebuild a studied screen.** When the product is of the same kind as a screen in the study (a
208	finance home, a deploy overview), its arrangement is the trap: judges recognised the copies at once.
209	Take the structure from the product's own things instead: for a couple's budget, Mia, Joint and Tom
210	as three columns running through accounts, plan and bills; for a running club, the pace groups.
211	
212	Then list the screen's blocks as the answers to its next questions, one line each, the way the page
213	run lists claims. A block with no question is deleted. This is how you avoid the stock order of KPI
214	row, big chart, two small charts, table.
215	
216	Three more lines, each tested:
217	
218	- **Everything the brief names is on the first screen.** At 1440×900, every block the brief asks for
219	  shows its header and its first rows or its figure. Size the headline block to the question (about
220	  200-360px tall), cap long lists at 4-6 rows with "View all", and put time-sensitive blocks (bills
221	  due, SLAs running out, a failed deploy) before long tables. A chart whose line is flat for most of
222	  the window does not get the full width: give it two-thirds and put the next answer beside it.
223	- **The most frequent job is one click away.** Name it ("pack the orders due today", "reply to the
224	  oldest breach", "redeploy the failed build") and put its control where the answer shows: a primary
225	  button in the title row, an action on the row that needs it, a "View logs" on the failed item. A
226	  screen with no control for its main job reads as a report, not as a tool.
227	- **Show the evidence beside the answer.** A judge trusts "Error rate 0.28%" more with its spike
228	  annotated ("peaked at 3.9% after the 23:28 deploy, reverted") than with the number alone. One line
229	  of explanation on the event that matters is worth more than a second chart.
230	
231	### 2.3 Choose a style
232	
233	```bash
234	node <skill>/scripts/draw.mjs --app --kind <kind> --brief "<one line about the product>" \
235	  --screens <screens> [--theme light|dark] [--keep palette,type] --options 3
236	```
237	
238	This deals up to three styles from `library/app.json` (fewer when only two suit the kind and the
239	theme). `draw.mjs --app --list kinds` (or `styles`, `screens` or `signatures`) prints the choices; the
240	screens are `overview`, `analytics`, `list`, `detail`, `settings`, `wallet`,
241	`builder`, `inbox`, `home` and `report`. The library holds seven styles, each distilled from the
242	studied screens that share its move:
243	
244	| Style | Theme | For | The move |
245	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
246	| `achromatic-ledger` | light | money homes, reports, settings with usage | No colour in the chrome; charts in ink; one small signal where a figure changed |
247	| `framed-sheet` | light | B2B analytics, developer platforms, builders | One tinted L-frame; the page on a white sheet inset 8px, no shadow |
248	| `accent-ladder` | light | creator and small-business admin with plans | The full hue on small marks only; its pale tints on every area |
249	| `editorial-greeting` | light | team and personal homes | The greeting as the h1 in a centred 12-column column; every figure at regular weight |
250	| `pastel-consumer` | light | wallets, budgeting | Pale same-hue tiles under one large radius; quiet money polarity |
251	| `true-black-flat` | dark | community, events, media | Elevation by lightness alone; colour only on data |
252	| `data-terminal` | dark | markets, monitoring | Every selection is the same 1px accent line; signs, not colour, on numbers |
253	
254	Choose by how the product is used (long sessions or a quick look, money or media, a team or one
255	person, day or night), not by what is most familiar, and write one line on why. Then deal the sheet:
256	
257	```bash
258	node <skill>/scripts/draw.mjs --app <the same arguments, without --options> --style <id>
259	```
260	
261	The sheet gives the style's tokens and type, its shell and one pattern for each screen you named.
262	Keep the style's one move intact and take every other value from the defaults in this file. Redraw
263	(`--redraw style | shell | screen:<name>`) only for a reason you can state: it contradicts the brand,
264	or the product is used in a way the style does not suit. With an existing brand, pass
265	`--keep palette,type`, map its colours onto the roles in §9 and keep the style's colour budget.
266	
267	**Then choose its face, before any markup.** The sheet's "Its face" list gives two or three ways this
268	style takes a face from the brief, and "Signature elements" lists the library's elements whose words
269	appear in the brief (a power flow for an energy home, a sell-out strip for a bakery, a cover matrix
270	and a kind-encoded timeline for a leave planner). Write in your notes, next to the screen's question:
271	the face you chose, the signature element (from the sheet, or your own built from the product's
272	things), and where each appears on the first screen. A style dealt to two products must not give them
273	the same face: in four rounds, the screens that skipped this step were scored as the same kit.
274	
275	### 2.4 Build the shell
276	
277	Build the frame first, empty: the sidebar or rail, the top bar if the shell has one, the canvas with
278	its gutters, the title row (§3 and §4). `<skill>/assets/app.css` is a neutral start for all of it:
279	copy it into the project and put the sheet's tokens in its `:root`. Look at it at 1440 and at 390 before any data goes in. Do the
280	grid arithmetic now and write it in a comment: the column count, the gutter, and the sum that proves
281	the cards land on the canvas edges.
282	
283	### 2.5 Put in the data
284	
285	Render every block from the dataset; draw the charts from it too, with `<skill>/assets/charts.js`
286	(`Charts.line`, `Charts.bars`, `Charts.diverging`, `Charts.ring`, `Charts.barList`, `Charts.plan`,
287	`Charts.bullet`, `Charts.timeline`, `Charts.matrix`, `Charts.timeStrip`; the file's header lists their
288	options) or your own SVG to the rules of §6, never a chart library's defaults and never a picture of a
289	chart. The newer helpers return `{ svg, legend }`: put that legend in the card's header rather than
290	drawing your own, so each swatch is the mark it explains. Format every figure by §7.4: separators, fixed decimals per
291	metric, a sign on every change, units as smaller grey suffixes, tabular figures, right alignment in
292	columns. Use the product's own words for labels. No placeholder data: the inspector fails lorem ipsum,
293	Acme, John Doe and their kind. Proof is not invented here either: no vanity totals, no "+12%" on an
294	account that is a week old.
295	
296	### 2.6 Build the states
297	
298	For every block, build its empty, zero, loading and error state (§11); for every row and control, its
299	hover, selected, focus and disabled state. Look at each one in the browser. A screen that only works
300	with full data is half built.
301	
302	### 2.7 The check
303	
304	```bash
305	node <skill>/scripts/lint.mjs --app <source files or folder>
306	node <skill>/scripts/inspect.mjs --app <url or path/to/index.html>
307	```
308	
309	A sheet dealt with `--app` switches both tools to the app rules by itself. The inspector opens the
310	screen at 1440, 768 and 390 and measures what this chapter asks for: an h1 (and reports it as the
311	screen's hero); a sidebar that folds on the phone; the canvas used to its right edge; panel shadows
312	and borders; the number of corner radii; cards in one row that end apart, where a column of cards
313	stacked with the gutter counts as one block (`ragged-row`); a blank band inside a card of over 40px,
314	or over 64px before a new section's heading (`panel-void`); icons in tinted squares; numeric alignment and tabular figures; chart hues; colour
315	share, and a screen with charts but no hue on its data (`no-data-hue`); placeholder data; text under
316	11px; and the page rules that still hold (contrast, gradients, the banned palettes, emoji). Fix every
317	`FAIL`. Treat each `WARN` as wrong unless you can defend it to a designer in one sentence.
318	
319	Then look at the screenshots, every width, and answer these in writing. This is the critique for an
320	app screen: the caps in `critique.md` for pictures, motion and the page's live element are page rules
321	and do not apply here.
322	
323	1. Is the screen's question answered by the biggest thing on it, and is that read first? Is the
324	   largest figure the one that answers the title row's sentence?
325	2. Does every block share the screen's edges? Is there a dead strip on one side, a card stopping
326	   short, an orphan cell, a stretched card with a blank band (a legend pinned to its foot, four rows
327	   in a card kept at its neighbour's height)?
328	3. Is colour only on data, on status and on the one primary action, and does the main data element
329	   carry the one hue? Does the face you chose show on the first screen?
330	4. Do the numbers add up, and do they line up digit for digit? List every fact that appears twice
331	   and check that the copies agree; recompute each total and change from the values as displayed;
332	   check that every relative figure names what it is against.
333	5. Does every zero look like a zero and every missing value like a dash? Does every count badge sit
334	   on a queue that needs action, with its noun clear from the label?
335	6. Does every legend swatch match the mark it explains, and does any caption have to say which bars
336	   are which (then encode it in the chart)? Does any label collide with a line or another label?
337	7. On the phone, is the navigation folded away, and does each block still answer its question?
338	
339	Fix the worst three, inspect again, look again. Three rounds at most. Judge the pictures: if a problem
340	shows in a screenshot, it is real, whatever the code says.
341	
342	### 2.8 Report
343	
344	Tell the user, briefly: the style dealt (name and seed) and any redraws with their reasons; the face
345	you chose and the signature element; each screen's one question; any check you allowed and why (for example `--allow icon-chips` for node-type
346	tiles in a builder); and the sample data that must be replaced with real data, listed so it can be
347	found.
348	
349	App screens have no motion floor. Motion is feedback: press, hover, focus, a menu or a sheet opening,
350	a row arriving. Nothing on the screen performs an entrance (house rule).
351	
352	## 3. The shell
353	
354	### 3.1 Five archetypes
355	
356	| Shell | In the study | What it is |
357	| --- | --- | --- |
358	| **Open plane** | 5 screens | A labelled sidebar on the page ground (or within 1-2% of it), separated by nothing or by one 1px hairline. No top bar: the header and the cards sit on the ground. The canvas is fluid with a 24-64px gutter, or a centred column. |
359	| **Tinted frame, white sheet** | 8 screens | Sidebar and top bar share one tinted ground (#f6f6f6-#f9fbfc) with no rule between them; the page sits on a white sheet inset 8px from the window's right and bottom edges, radius 10-16 (median 16), a 1px #eaeaea-#ededed edge and no shadow. Variants: a flush L-frame, the inset sheet, and floating panels inset 8-12px with a 12px gap. |
360	| **Ruled T-frame** | 4 screens | A 210-240px sidebar and a 64px top bar on one ground, divided only by 1px rules. The workspace switcher sits at the top bar's right end behind a full-height divider. Three of the four are dark. |
361	| **Icon rail** | 3 screens | An unlabelled rail 50-60px wide (median 55); 15-18px icons on a 34-49px pitch; the active item marked by colour or by a 2% tint band; groups split by 20px hairlines. It saves about 180px of width. |
362	| **No sidebar** | 3 screens | A 46-48px top bar over a centred 1088-1208px column with 152-212px gutters; the logo sits on the column's left edge. For reports, viewers and products with few destinations. |
363	
364	All six dark screens use one ground everywhere, divided by 1px rules of #161616-#232323 or by nothing.
365	No screen in the study puts a dark or saturated sidebar against a light canvas (0 of 17).
366	
367	### 3.2 Sidebar
368	
369	- **Width.** Labelled sidebars run 210-292px; the median is 230 and most sit at 224-240. One floating
370	  sidebar card appears (280px wide, 40px in from the window edge).
371	- **Rows.** A 32px hit area on a 34px pitch is the mode (7 screens); the roomy versions run 40-52px on
372	  a 42-60px pitch. Icons are 14-20px, median 16, outline at about 1.5px stroke on 14 of 16 screens.
373	  Labels are 14px at 400 on 12 of 16, in ink or in a grey of #4b4d4f-#63666e, about 8-10px after the
374	  icon, with the label column at x 36-48.
375	- **Active item.** A neutral grey pill with the label unchanged, on 8 screens: radius 4-16 (median 8),
376	  inset 8-14px from the sidebar's edges, a fill of about #e9e9e9-#ededed. On dark, brightness alone:
377	  the label goes from #bbb to #fff (3 screens). Colour alone on the icon or label (3, all of them
378	  rails or a floating card). A tinted accent fill (3). A left accent bar once in 23. The weight
379	  changes on 2. Default: the grey pill on light, brightness on dark.
380	- **Groups.** Sentence-case grey labels at 12-13px, never uppercase (9 screens), with 22-56px of air
381	  above and 13-33px to the first item; or hairlines instead (4). Utilities such as settings and help
382	  pushed to the bottom (5).
383	- **Top and bottom.** The workspace or account switcher at the top of the sidebar (7 screens), at its
384	  bottom (2), or in the top bar. The bottom holds a user row (8) or one upsell (8); one of those
385	  upsells is a filled accent button.
386	- **The product is named** (house rule, from testing). The product's mark and name sit at the top of
387	  the sidebar or rail, and the scope (workspace, team, project, account) is shown as a switcher or a
388	  breadcrumb. A screen whose product cannot be named from the screenshot reads as a template.
389	- **Counts on nav items** (house rule, from testing). A count appears only on a queue that needs
390	  action, and its noun is clear from the label: "Requests 5", "Price changes 3". A bare "Range and
391	  prices 9" left the judge asking nine of what.
392	- **Labels by default.** A labelled sidebar unless the product has five destinations or fewer and the
393	  screen needs the width (a research or monitoring view); an icon rail always carries the product's
394	  mark at the top, a tooltip and an accessible name on every icon. Nav items are other screens, never
395	  anchors into the current page (a sidebar that scroll-spies one long page was marked down twice).
396	
397	### 3.3 Top bar
398	
399	14 of 23 screens have one; the default is none. Heights fall into two groups: 44-51px (median about
400	48) on light chrome, and 64px, usually with a 1px rule. A top bar must hold something real: search,
401	the workspace switcher, or the page or object name. Search sits centred on the window at 548x32 with
402	a shortcut hint (2 screens), or at 457-537x36 in a no-sidebar bar. The right cluster is inset 24-46px
403	from the edge. Two screens leave about 1070px of their top bar blank; both are flagged for it.
404	
405	### 3.4 Right rail and pinned columns
406	
407	One screen has a right rail: a fixed 384px column in a `1fr 384px` grid with a 24px gap, starting
408	level with the first card rather than with the title, its section headings outside the cards and 8px
409	above each. Use one only for a stable secondary stream: recent items, the details of the selected
410	object, share links. A pinned left column appears once: a 306px accounts card at the viewport height
411	minus 72px, so net worth stays in view while the rest of the screen scrolls.
412	
413	Five screens float a button (24-56px), and one of those buttons covers the content it sits on and is
414	flagged. House rule: no floating button unless it is the screen's one primary action and covers
415	nothing at any width.
416	
417	## 4. The canvas and the page title
418	
419	### 4.1 Width and gutters
420	
421	- **Fluid** (14 screens): side padding 17-64px, median 29, with 24 and 36-40 the common values;
422	  content 1120-1312px wide, median about 1204.
423	- **Centred** (8 screens): 624, 864, 1088, 1100, 1152, about 1190 and 1208px; median about 1126.
424	  Data pages land at 1100-1250 either way. Only two personal homes go narrow (624 and 864), and both
425	  are flagged for wasting the width.
426	- **Top offset**, from the canvas top to the title: 20-88px, median about 36. Tools sit at 20-36;
427	  greeting homes at 50-88.
428	- **One gutter.** Use one gap value horizontally and vertically. Mixed gutters (12 against 16, 20
429	  against 24, 16 against 12) are flagged on 8 screens.
430	
431	### 4.2 One left edge, one right edge
432	
433	The strongest screens run a single left edge from the header to the last row. One indents its page
434	header by the cards' 24px padding, so the title, the card titles, the numbers and the chart all start
435	on one line. Row rules may bleed 7-8px past the text column while the text stays on it.
436	
437	The grid's arithmetic closes: 3 x 372 + 2 x 17 = 2 x 568 + 16 = 1152; 12 x 77 + 11 x 16 = 1100;
438	4 x 144 + 3 x 16 = 624; a second-row card exactly as wide as the two cards above it
439	(251 + 24 + 515). Write your sum down.
440	
441	Failures to avoid, all from the study: cards stopping 120px short of the sheet's right edge; a 0px
442	right gutter against a 40px left one; a column centred on the window instead of on the area beside
443	the sidebar (204px on its left, 444px on its right); a medallion 108px off the column's axis. The
444	inspector warns when the content stops well short of the right edge.
445	
446	**Dead space from a grid that does not fit the data** is the commonest failure in the study (10
447	screens): four KPI tiles in a three-column grid, orphaning the fourth; one card alone in a
448	three-column row beside 810px of nothing; a card stretched to its neighbour's height with 250px of
449	blank under its legend. Choose the column count from the number of items, let a lone card span, and
450	do not stretch a card's frame over empty space.
451	
452	**Cards that share a row share a bottom edge.** In testing, rows whose cards stopped 26-190px apart
453	were marked down every time, by judges and by the inspector (`ragged-row`). Balance the row by its
454	content first: move a list's rows so the two columns hold the same number, cap both lists at the same
455	count, or pair blocks of similar height. Two cards stacked in one column beside a tall card count as
456	one block: they balance when the column ends level. Only when the contents cannot balance, stack the
457	two blocks, or let the shorter card fill the row height with its content top-aligned and the footer
458	action (a "View all", a total) pinned to its bottom so the extra height is not a hole.
459	
460	**A stretched card stretches only when it has content to fill.** Only an action or a total may be
461	pinned to a stretched card's foot; a legend or a note stays directly under its chart. In testing, a
462	cover card stretched to its neighbour with its legend pinned to the bottom left 60px of blank under
463	the last row, and a sell-out card left 45px above its links. When the content is short, let the card
464	keep its own height (`align-items: start` on the row), move its footer link into its header, or give
465	the row a block of similar height. A filtered block shrinks to its rows, or keeps a fixed number of
466	rows with one sentence in the empty ones; four rows over 270px of empty card is a hole. The inspector
467	warns on a blank band of over 40px inside a card (`panel-void`).
468	
469	**Narrow blocks do not span the canvas.** A table of five columns or fewer, or a list of six rows or
470	fewer, runs to about 760px at 1440 and pairs with the next block; stretched to 1300px it leaves
471	400-600px voids between a name and its first figure.
472	
473	### 4.3 The title
474	
475	- **Every screen has one h1**; the inspector fails a screen without one. 14 screens set it in the
476	  canvas at 18-48px, median and mode 24, at 600-700 (700 on 8). The rest have nothing over 16px: a
477	  breadcrumb or the top bar names the page. Then the breadcrumb's last item is the h1, at 16px, and
478	  the screen's name is still the first thing read.
479	- **A noun, not a greeting**: "Analytics", "Overview", the project's or the object's name. 3 of 23
480	  greet, and one adds an emoji, which goes. A greeting suits a personal or team home only.
481	- **An optional second line**: one 14-16px grey sentence about the data or the object (the finding,
482	  the period, the scope), never about the interface ("the filters narrow every block…", "this page
483	  shows…" read as instructions, not a product), or a 12px line
484	  naming the data's source.
485	- **Right of the title**: actions only when they are real (10 screens); otherwise nothing. A freshness
486	  stamp ("Updated Jul 27, 4:09 PM", with a refresh button) on 6.
487	- **The primary action.** 12 of 23 have no filled primary button; 5 make it near-black (#1d1f20,
488	  #1f2937) or inverted white on dark; 4 fill it with the brand hue. One primary per screen.
489	
490	### 4.4 Tabs, filters and the date range
491	
492	- **The date range** at page level (7 screens) or on each card (7), never both. A card that states its
493	  own period puts it in its header, right-aligned, in grey.
494	- **Underline tabs** (8 screens) always sit on a full-width 1px rule; the indicator is 1-4px (median
495	  2), as wide as the label or running 8-11px past it.
496	- **A segmented track** once: 48px, #f3f4f6, a white 36px active pill, and the date select inside its
497	  right end, so tabs and range read as one row. A segmented control is as wide as its options, and full
498	  width only below about 480px: three options spread across a 680px tablet card read as a progress bar.
499	- **Control height** in title and filter rows: 28-40px, median 34, clustering at 32 and 36.
500	- **Order**: scope on the left (the date first, then the filters), utility and refresh on the right.
501	- **Compound filters** that read as a sentence ("Date | Jun 14 - Jul 13 | Daily"), 28px tall and 8px
502	  apart, once.
503	- **To the first card**: 13-64px, median 24.
504	
505	## 5. KPIs
506	
507	- **No tile of its own.** 11 of the 20 screens with headline numbers give a KPI no tile: bare text on
508	  the page or on a card (5), or one container split by 1px hairlines (6). 9 use one card per KPI,
509	  61-147px tall (median about 108). The default is one container split by 1px dividers into equal
510	  columns. 7 screens have no KPI row at all and put each headline number in the card that explains
511	  it, which is often better.
512	- **Count.** 1-6 per row, median 3-4. The count matches the grid: four KPIs get four columns.
513	- **Size.** Values 16-40px, median 26, mode 24. Values in their own tile run larger (median 30) than
514	  in a shared strip (median 24). Nothing at 48px or over. Labels 12-16px, median 14; the value is
515	  about 1.7 times the label.
516	- **Weight.** An even split: 400 on 8 screens, 600 on 6, 700-800 on 6. A large number at regular
517	  weight under a semibold label is the common pattern. Bold for money only.
518	- **Order.** Label above the value on 14 screens; labels grey (#6b6b6b-#aaa) on 13; sentence case.
519	- **Nothing else.** No icon in a coloured circle (0 of 23), no sparkline (0 of 23), no tinted tile.
520	  An info icon beside the label is fine (5 screens). Units are a smaller grey suffix: "5 mins" at 24
521	  over 14, "2 m 24 s", "5 /10".
522	- **The answer figure leads.** When one figure is the screen's answer (a balance, net worth, the
523	  portfolio's value), it is 30-36px and at least 1.3 times its sibling figures (those at 18-24px). In
524	  testing, a 24px portfolio value beside two 24px figures left the screen without a lead. No other
525	  figure on the screen is larger: the biggest number answers the title row's sentence, so a
526	  secondary ratio in another card stays at the siblings' size.
527	- **One figure, one place.** A figure shown in the strip is not repeated in a legend beside it, and a
528	  KPI strip whose every cell names a panel below (RSVPs, then an RSVPs panel) is dropped: lead each
529	  panel with its own number instead.
530	- **A second job.** KPIs may be the chart's series tabs or the list's type filter (the selected card
531	  takes a 1.5px border). As tabs, the selected one carries a 2px rule or the active fill and an ink
532	  label; the others keep a grey label and their value in ink, at 400 against the selected one's 500.
533	  A grey value reads as disabled: in testing, three shops' takings set in grey because they were tabs
534	  read as secondary, though they were the brief's first ask. When the tabs are the per-entity
535	  breakdown the brief asks for, grey nothing and let the rule alone mark the selection. On a phone the
536	  tabs become a 2-up grid with the selected cell filled, or a row that scrolls sideways; never an
537	  underline floating inside the grid (`app.css` does both).
538	
539	### Deltas
540	
541	- Optional: 9 of the 20 KPI screens show one; 11 do not.
542	- 10-15px (median 14), never larger than the label. Text or a small glyph on 6 screens; a pale pill
543	  on 3.
544	- **The window in words**: "vs prior 30 days", "in the last 90 days", "from 0 (last 4 weeks)" (7 of
545	  the 9).
546	- **Colour only the number**, or set the whole delta in grey.
547	- **Colour says good or bad, not up or down** (house rule, from testing). Every metric has a good
548	  direction: latency, error rate, cost, churn and time-to-reply are better when they fall. A change
549	  in the bad direction puts `--negative` on the number (or a small down-pointing glyph in that
550	  colour); a change in the good direction is `--positive` or grey. A judge read a 2.5× rise in errors
551	  set in the same grey as a rise in visits as hiding the screen's only bad news.
552	- **Zero or undefined change is grey.** The study's commonest KPI failure is a zero or undefined change
553	  shown as a signal: three identical green "up 100%" pills grown from zero, a ">999%", a bold red
554	  "0.00%", a green "+0". When the prior period was zero, write "+4 (new)"; when there is nothing to
555	  compare, a short grey dash where the delta would be.
556	
557	## 6. Charts
558	
559	### 6.1 Which chart for which question
560	
561	| Question | Form | In the study |
562	| --- | --- | --- |
563	| Is it moving over time? | One line; an area only with a fill of 15% or less | 9 screens |
564	| How much per period? | Columns with square corners | 3 |
565	| How is it distributed? | A histogram with equal bins | 1 (its unequal bins are flagged) |
566	| Who ranks? | A sorted horizontal bar list, or the row's fill as the bar in a one-figure list | 3 |
567	| What share? | A thin ring, or a 100% stacked bar with 2px seams; five parts at most | 5 |
568	| How far to the target? | A progress bar, both ends labelled, the fill the true ratio | 4 |
569	| How much of the plan is used? | A track as long as the plan, the spent part filled, what is already committed as a lighter segment, an overrun past the track's end in the negative colour (`Charts.plan`) | house rule |
570	| Has it drifted from its target? | One row per part: the current share as a bar with a 1px tick at the target (`Charts.bullet`); never two stacked bars to compare | house rule |
571	| Where? | A map with a list beside it; the list carries the magnitudes | 1 |
572	| Per period, and the running total? | The two side by side at equal width, with the same dates | 1 |
573	| Which way did it flow, and how much? | Columns above and below one zero line on one scale, the axis signed and captioned on each side ("Sold" above, "Bought" below), a marked period in a second tone with its own legend entry (`Charts.diverging`) | house rule |
574	| Who is away when? | A timeline of people by day, each kind of booking its own mark (`Charts.timeline`) | house rule |
575	| Is there enough cover? | A team-by-day matrix of slack against the minimum (+2, +1, 0, −1), one hue ramping toward the negative colour, the headcount on hover (`Charts.matrix`) | house rule |
576	| When in the day, against last time? | One row per item on a shared opening-to-closing axis: a 2px grey track, an ink dot for today, a hollow tick for the comparison day (`Charts.timeStrip`) | house rule |
577	
578	Three more, from testing:
579	
580	- **The pair of per-period bars and the running total is used once per screen**, and only when the
581	  total crosses a line that matters (capacity, a target). Three such pairs in six charts read as one
582	  pattern stamped out.
583	- **A series that is flat except for one event** gets at most two-thirds of the width and about 140px of
584	  height, or a range capped at about twice its reference line with the off-scale peak labelled
585	  (`Charts.line({ max })`). A full-width plot that is 85% empty was the biggest block on a first
586	  screen and was marked down.
587	- **A forecast is not a fact**: after today the line is dashed and the end value is labelled
588	  (`Charts.line({ today, endLabel })`), with the gap to the target bracketed when there is one.
589	- **What the brief asks to see over time is drawn on the first screen.** KPI cells may switch the chart
590	  only between metrics the brief did not name.
591	
592	When there are only a few numbers, draw no chart: four screens skip it, and the settings page links
593	to the analytics screen with "View more".
594	
595	### 6.2 One question, one series
596	
597	One series per chart is the norm; three is the most any screen draws. To show another metric, switch
598	it with a control (a segmented control, a dropdown, the KPIs as tabs) instead of overlaying lines.
599	Plots run 112-264px tall (median about 195) and 316-1136px wide (median about 570), an aspect of 1.8
600	to 5.2.
601	
602	### 6.3 Axes and gridlines
603	
604	- **Gridlines** run horizontally only on 7 of the 12 cartesian charts, both ways on 3, and not at all
605	  on 2. Use 3-5 (the study runs 3-7, median 4-5): 1px, solid, about #e5e5e5 on light (range
606	  #cfcfd2-#f2f2f2), #2b2b2b on #111. Dashed lines are allowed in chart grids (4 screens: 3/3, 4/4,
607	  3/2.5) and nowhere else on the screen.
608	- **No y-axis line.** The baseline is the one heavier line (2px on two screens, 1px on one); full axes
609	  on one.
610	- **Y ticks**: 4-7, median 5, at 11-16px (median 12) in grey (#5f5f5f-#6c6c6c), on the left (8
611	  screens) or the right (2). Round, even steps (0/5/10/15%; 0-600 by 150), the top tick above the
612	  maximum, integers for counts, and zero as the baseline for bars and counts.
613	- **Never without a scale.** Two screens draw no y-scale and show magnitude only on hover; both are
614	  flagged. So are uneven ticks (0/3/6/10), a 0.8 tick on a count, a top tick equal to the maximum so
615	  the line hits the plot's edge, and a cumulative axis that starts at 1.
616	- **Axis text no larger than the data.** 15-16px ticks beside 14px values are flagged as louder than
617	  the numbers.
618	- **X labels**: 4-8 per chart, flat, never rotated (40 degrees is flagged), the first and last pulled
619	  inside the plot, on one step all the way: a forced closing label after 14:00 on a 90-minute step
620	  left a short last gap that a judge measured. Choose a step that lands on the end (hourly from 08:00
621	  to 15:00) or leave the end unlabelled. Labelling only the two ends hides when things happened. Irregular dates on a
622	  categorical axis are flagged: time goes on a time scale.
623	
624	### 6.4 Marks
625	
626	- **Lines** 1-3px, median 2, in straight segments. Four screens smooth their lines, and one smoothed
627	  curve invents values between daily totals (flagged), so draw straight segments. No point markers,
628	  except a hover dot (8px on one screen).
629	- **Fill**: none on 7 of 10 time charts. At most a flat tint of about 14%, or a fade from the line to
630	  transparent over 150-200px.
631	- **Bars** have square corners (4 screens), or at most a 4px top radius with a square bottom on the
632	  baseline. Stacked segments are split by a 1-2px seam.
633	- **Colour.** One hue per chart. The accent touches only data on 8 screens, and data ink is under 3%
634	  of the pixels on most. Neutral series are fine and often better: a near-black line that turns pale
635	  grey after the cursor; a white line against a red one; signs instead of colour ("+$24,000,000").
636	  But the one hue, when the style has one, goes on the screen's main data element (today's series,
637	  the booked bars, the current period, the margin that breaks), not on a secondary chart or a delta:
638	  in testing, an all-ink screen with no hue on any of its data read as a kit.
639	  One subject keeps one hue across the screen: the same subscribers drawn pink in one chart and indigo
640	  in the next is flagged. Unrelated hues on one screen (three, five) are flagged every time. Status
641	  colours are for status. The inspector warns over four hues and fails over six.
642	- **Legends.** None for a single series (9 charts): the title or the dropdown names it. Otherwise five
643	  items at most, as a 5-8px dot with a 12-14px grey label in the card's header, or as a small table
644	  (dot, name, value, change) that makes the legend carry data. Never list a series that has no data
645	  (flagged). Every swatch is the mark it explains, scaled down: the legend dot is the line's colour,
646	  a hatched bar's swatch is hatched. A swatch drawn separately from the mark drifted from it in testing
647	  (a black outline with a red edge explaining a red outline); the helpers return the legend built from
648	  the same style object as the marks.
649	- **Rings** only for three to five parts of a whole that are not already listed beside them (a ring
650	  redrawing the spent, due and left figures of the tile next to it was marked redundant). Never
651	  labelled on the slices; the total sits in the centre or beside the ring. The
652	  screens noted for their rings use thin strokes: 3-5px on a 90-154px ring, 8px on 182px. Two others
653	  use 28 and 37px.
654	- **Progress bars** are 4-24px tall (median 8), fully rounded, with both ends labelled ("Skilled 200"
655	  and "Expert 2,000"); the fill is the true ratio, so 303 on that scale fills 22px of 392. A zero has
656	  no stub (a 6px stub at zero is flagged).
657	- **Tooltips** are bare text or a plain box without an arrow: label and value on one line.
658	- **Annotate the event that matters.** A step or a spike more than about three times the usual change
659	  gets a 1px marker and a 12px label naming its cause ("Deploy a3f09c1", "Newsletter featured");
660	  reference lines (a budget, an SLO, a start time) are 1px dashed with their label at the end. In
661	  testing, an unexplained jump was the first thing a judge asked about. `Charts.line`,
662	  `Charts.bars` and `Charts.diverging` take `annotations` and `reference`.
663	- **Labels never collide.** Annotation labels sit in rows above the plot, each beside the top of its
664	  own leader line, and no leader line runs through another label; the rows are reserved only when a
665	  label exists, so a chart without one has no dead band above it. The "Now" label of a forecast goes
666	  on whichever side of its line the series does not cross. Lay labels out after the fonts load, or
667	  the label set changes between loads (it did in testing). The helpers do all of this; give a label
668	  that may not fit a `short` form.
669	- **Use the helper, then extend it.** Draw charts with `assets/charts.js` and add what a chart needs to
670	  it, rather than writing new axis code: in testing, every chart written from scratch on a phone put
671	  its y labels on top of its line.
672	- **Short and empty histories are drawn honestly**: a flat zero line with one spike, missing bars for
673	  empty periods, no padded y-range, no "No data" picture. Do not give one point the screen's largest
674	  plot, though: a lone dot in a full-size grid reads as barren (flagged once).
675	
676	## 7. Tables and lists
677	
678	### 7.1 Rows
679	
680	- Single-line data rows: 36-53px, median 45.
681	- Two-line rows with media: 56-92px, median 72. The pitch is the media's height plus 24-32px
682	  (48 + 24, 48 + 32, 50 + 30).
683	- Key-value and legend rows inside cards: 21-32px.
684	- In a two-line cell, line 2 sits about 21px below line 1 (19-23), one size smaller (12-14px) and
685	  grey. Two-line labels need a 40-44px pitch at least: on a 32px pitch a subline nearly touched the
686	  next row's name and the list ran together (house rule, from testing).
687	- Overview lists show 2-5 rows.
688	
689	### 7.2 Header
690	
691	- 11-14px, median 12, mostly regular weight, grey, sentence case (9 of the 11 headed tables). The one
692	  uppercase header in the study is flagged as louder than the data.
693	- **No fill band** (0 of 11) and **no rule under it** on 8 of 11. Where there is a rule, it is the
694	  strongest line in the table (#e5e7eb over #f3f4f6 row rules).
695	- Header row 36-40px.
696	- Numeric headers are right-aligned and flush with their values; a header that stops 15px short of
697	  its column is flagged. A header over a control aligns with the control it labels (centred over a
698	  column of steppers), and a delta beside a stepper gets its own narrow unlabelled column; three
699	  alignments in one header row were flagged.
700	- A sort glyph on the active column only.
701	
702	### 7.3 Dividers
703	
704	- **No zebra striping** (0 of 23).
705	- No row dividers on about half the lists; they rely on a 61-92px pitch or on 2-8px gaps between
706	  filled rows.
707	- When present: 1px, 3-7% darker than the surface (#ededed-#f4f4f4 on white; #161616 on #000,
708	  #1b1a1f on #131217).
709	- Extent: bleeding 8-9px past the text edge; starting at the text column and skipping the media; or
710	  the full inner width. Pick one per screen.
711	
712	### 7.4 Figures and alignment
713	
714	- **Numbers right-aligned**, in tabular figures or a monospace. Every left-aligned numeric column and
715	  every column of proportional digits in the study is flagged (durations "00:00:12" and "00:00:04"
716	  that jitter, cents that drift).
717	- **Fixed decimals per metric**: money 2, percentages 1 or 2, counts none. Thousands separators
718	  everywhere ("$16,531.54"); abbreviate only in a capacity line ("12.7k of 20.0k"). A sign on every
719	  change ("-$0.09", "+10,100 (+0.20%)"). No space after the currency sign (one screen's "$ 89.00"
720	  beside "$15.00" is flagged).
721	- **The identity column gets the most width**, about a third to a half of the table, and it is never
722	  the one cut off at desktop width: shorten names editorially first (drop the issuer every row
723	  shares, the share class, "Ltd") and use the same short name at every width.
724	- **One right edge per row or card**: every right-aligned figure inside a card or row ends on the same
725	  padding line (a days-in-stage figure 18px short of the value above it reads as a second edge).
726	- **Two measures stack in one cell** rather than taking two columns: a count over its 12px grey
727	  percentage, a date over its time, a money value over the amount in units, both lines on one right
728	  edge.
729	- **Dates** in ISO form and right-aligned where rows are compared ("2024-02-15"); in words for
730	  recency ("Today", "Yesterday", "6 days").
731	- **IDs** in a monospace at body size, truncated to about 8 characters with an ellipsis and a copy
732	  icon 12px after.
733	- Truncate to one line with an ellipsis; never break inside a word.
734	- **A breakdown in a narrow card** ("Headingley 6 · Chapel Allerton 5 · Meanwood 3") goes in fixed
735	  mini-columns, or each item is `nowrap` with its separator attached to the next item, so no line ends
736	  on a dangling "·".
737	- **An edited cell shows that it changed** (house rule, from testing). In an editable grid a changed
738	  value carries a mark (a dot, a tinted border), and the column header or a caption names the
739	  baseline ("vs the usual Monday"); a bare grey "+5" beside a stepper was read as noise.
740	
741	### 7.5 Ink inside rows
742	
743	- Only the identity and the key number get the primary ink; everything else is grey ("5" in ink,
744	  " /10" in grey).
745	- A missing value is a grey dash; a real zero is printed ("$0", "0.00%", "0% (0)").
746	- The sign lives in the text, not in the colour: income green with a "+", expenses in ink, no red on
747	  every negative.
748	- Link colour on the name cell only, with no underline.
749	
750	### 7.6 Status pills
751	
752	- 15-28px tall (median 20), text 9-14px in the study (median 12) at 500; nothing under 11px here. A
753	  full pill or a 3-5px tag.
754	- A pale tint with dark text of the same hue, optionally a 1px border one step darker: #dcfae5 with
755	  #04250e, #ffedea with #831c1e.
756	- Neutral states are monochrome chips with a glyph ("Public" with a globe).
757	- A state machine uses one hue at three intensities: grey for off, the full hue for the call to
758	  action, a dark tint for running. A saturated fill with white text only for that one call to action,
759	  and only while it is rare: when more than about a fifth of the visible rows carry it, it becomes a
760	  stripe of black blobs louder than the data (marked down in testing); use the pale pair or a 6px dot
761	  with an ink label instead.
762	- **One status mark per row.** A tag and a badge that say the same thing are flagged.
763	- **A chip is never squeezed.** Tags and pills are `flex: none; white-space: nowrap`: in testing a
764	  table column collapsed an environment chip to a 12px box with its word spilling out.
765	
766	### 7.7 Media
767	
768	16px logos in dense rows; 24-32px avatars; 48-50px in two-line rows. Circles for people, tokens and
769	companies; a 2-3px radius for artwork and flags; 8px for photographs. One fixed media slot down the
770	list so the text starts on one edge (a 50px slot with the text 16px after it). Media-to-text gap
771	10-16px, median 12.
772	
773	### 7.8 Actions and paging
774	
775	- **No pagination on an overview** (0 of 23). Cap the rows and link out: "View all" in the section
776	  header, a 30px outlined button under the list, a full-width 32px bar. State the total ("3 tracks").
777	- Row actions: none on 9 screens; otherwise one kebab at the far right. Reserve a trailing action
778	  column only when most rows carry the action; otherwise the action is an ink text action on the
779	  row's second line and the figures stay flush to the card edge. When a row needs doing
780	  (a bill to pay, an order to pack, a failed deploy), its action is a visible ghost button or an ink
781	  text action in one fixed trailing column, at the same pitch for every row; never muted grey text,
782	  and never stacked under the amount so the rows change height.
783	- Checkboxes only where bulk actions exist (one screen: 18px, 2px stroke, 3px radius).
784	- Hover and selected: a 1px outline at 6px radius overhanging the panel by 1px, or a darker border
785	  with a 1px ring. No hover that changes the fill was seen. In a list that drives a detail pane (an
786	  inbox, a queue), the selected row takes the `--active` fill of the nav pill instead, so it cannot be
787	  mistaken for a focus ring or a hover (house rule, from testing).
788	- Toolbar: one search, 30-36px tall (256x30, 252x36, 316x32).
789	- **A full list screen** (house rule; the study has none): state the total above the table, keep the
790	  header row in view while scrolling, and page or load more at the end with the range shown
791	  ("1-50 of 1,284").
792	
793	### 7.9 Lists that carry data
794	
795	- **The row fill is the bar**: the row's rounded background (radius 8) as wide as its share of the
796	  largest share; 44px rows, 2px gaps. Only in a one-figure ranking list (a label and one value): in a
797	  row with several columns or two lines, the fill's edge cuts through the words (failed in testing).
798	  Planned against spent is a separate 6-8px track under the label (`Charts.plan`).
799	- **Bar list**: a 64px pitch, a label line, then a 10px pill bar with the value 5px after its end; the
800	  longest bar about 88% of the width; one colour, no track.
801	- **Inline bars in a list are thin and grey** unless they are the screen's main series: 2-3px at
802	  most. A ranked list of money in a narrow card carries a 2px proportional bar under each label, grey
803	  with the top item in ink (`Charts.barList(el, rows, { thin: true })`), so "most costly first" is

805	- **A timeline draws its comparison.** When the brief asks "against last Sunday", the comparison is a
